name: Evergreen Park & Campground
note: Village of Wausaukee park of about 40 acres on the village's northeast edge, with the Wausaukee River, a class 2 trout stream, and Evergreen Park Pond on site.  Deluxe full-hookup sites and rustic electric ones; the showers take coins. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Read on the Campspot marketplace: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (Rustic RV Site, Deluxe Full Hookup Pull-Through RV Site and Deluxe Full Hookup RV Site). June 2027: $29-43, Tuesday and Saturday alike. Campspot shows the park closed in October 2026 and January 2027. Plus the park's $4 '$4 Transaction Fee', once per stay. Read 2026-10-13.

name: Hartwick Pines State Park Campground
note: Modern campground of Hartwick Pines State Park (9,335 acres, with the old-growth pines) near Grayling. Sites 1-64 have 20/30-amp electric with shared water spigots; sites 65-100 are full hookup with 50-amp. Trails from the campground to Bright and Glory lakes and a spur to the park's mountain-bike trails. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: 2027 on the booking site (2027-05-18 and 07-13 alike): 20/30-amp sites $43, full-hookup 50-amp sites $58. 2026: $41 / $56 on the booking site (2026-10-27); the DNR rates table lists $41 / $51. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.
field_notes.Sites: 100 sites: 1-64 20/30-amp electric, 65-100 full hookup with 50-amp (the booking site lists 63 electric-only and 37 sewer-hookup sites). Every site takes tents or a trailer/RV up to 40 ft on the booking site. Open-air, pull-through and wooded sites; four accessible sites (52, 54, 86, 87).

name: Muskegon State Park - Channel Campground
note: Modern campground in two loops by the Muskegon Lake navigation channel walkway: the first loop (sites 1-92) is adjacent to the channel, the second (sites 101-147) has larger sites near the big dune and Muskegon Lake. The channel walkway and its parking lot are closed for a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers project through Nov. 14, 2026 (DNR park page, read 2026-10-25). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757.
field_notes.Fees: 2027 on the booking site: $48 a night for the 108 20/30-amp sites, $53 for the 31 second-loop sites with 50-amp service (2027-05-18 and 07-13 alike). 2026: $45 / $50 (DNR rates table). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.
field_notes.Sites: 139 campsites: 93 in the first loop (sites 1-92, beside the navigation channel) and 46 in the second (101-147, larger sites near the dune and Muskegon Lake), every one with electric. Allowed rigs run up to 20-50 ft: the first loop is mostly 30-ft sites (67), the second mostly 45-50 ft; 33 sites take 50 ft. Ten pull-throughs (first loop 5, 8, 9, 18, 48, 53; second loop 131, 144, 146, 147).

name: Newaygo State Park Campground
note: Rustic campground in two loops (Oak #1-48, Poplar #49-99) atop 20-ft embankments overlooking Hardy Dam Pond, a 6-mile flooding of the Muskegon River; large private sites with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers. Boat launch between the loops with a few mooring spots for registered campers, buoyed swim area in the Poplar loop, kayak rentals at the office early June to mid-September, 18-hole disc golf; borders the Manistee National Forest. Spongy moth larvae can surge in summer. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night at every rustic site, in 2026 (DNR rates table) and on the booking site for May, July and November dates through 2027. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.
field_notes.Sites: 99 rustic campsites in two loops, Oak (#1-48) and Poplar (#49-99), with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers between them. Allowed rig lengths on the booking site run 25-50 ft; all but 3 take 30 ft or more. No pull-throughs listed.

name: Onaway State Park Campground
note: Modern campground on the southeast shore of Black Lake (Michigan's seventh-largest), with a cobblestone shoreline and rock outcroppings; the lower loop has sites on the lake, the upper loop sits on a bluff in white pines. Ocqueoc Falls is 10 mi east. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve online on MiDNRReservations or at 800-447-2757.
field_notes.Fees: 2027 on the booking site: $30 a night at every campsite (2027-05-18, 07-13, 10-26); 2026: $28 (DNR rates table, booking site 2026-10-27). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to all state park campgrounds.
field_notes.Sites: 82 electric campsites in a lower loop among cedars, with sites on the lake, and an upper loop in white pines (lake views from its east side), plus a camper cabin. Allowed rig lengths run 20-40 ft: 13 sites take only 20 ft, 18 take 35-40 ft. The shower building is a short walk from the lower loop.

name: Thunder Bay River State Forest Campground
note: Rustic MI DNR state forest campground on the banks of the Thunder Bay River, 9 mi SW of Alpena via M-32 and Indian Reserve Rd; the last stretch is a narrow gravel and dirt road. Undeveloped carry-in launch on the north side; pike, bass, walleye and panfish; also reachable by canoe. The 1.5-mile Wah-Wah-Tas-See Pathway starts here, and an ORV/snowmobile trailhead to the Devil's Loop trail adjoins the campground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The DNR amenity table gives seasonal closure dates of Dec 1 to May 1.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: Ten sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (no length posted) at the end of a narrow gravel and dirt road; water access at every site. One camping unit and six people per site.

name: Upper Manistee River State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground among red pines and hardwoods along the Upper Manistee River, 7.7 mi SW of Frederic via County Road 612 and Goose Creek Road; a narrow footpath runs along the water's edge, with a staircase to the river mid-campground and a path by site #16. Separate walk-in tent sites (parked a quarter mile SE) and a paddle-in/walk-in group area. Brown, brook and rainbow trout. The reservable Manistee backcountry/canoe sites are a separate USFS program. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground roads may not be plowed in winter.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: 30 sites 'for tent, small trailer and large trailer use'; walk-in sites (parking a quarter mile SE of the main entrance) and a paddle-in/walk-in group-use area are extra. One camping unit and six people per site.

name: Muskrat Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on shallow, warm-water Muskrat Lake, 12 mi NW of Mio via M-33 North, West Miller Road, Richardson Road and Muskrat Lake Road. Two sites accommodate a 40-ft vehicle/trailer (per an earlier DNR listing). Carry-in access to the lake; ORVs may ride between the campground and the trails (Mio ATV trail). Managed by Rifle River Recreation Area. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground roads may not be plowed in winter.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night (DNR amenity table). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: '13 sites for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording). The 40-ft maximum comes from an earlier note citing a DNR listing that two sites take a 40-ft vehicle/trailer; neither the current page nor its June 2025 version states it.

name: Silver Creek State Forest Campground
note: Quiet, shaded campground on the banks of the Pine River near the Silver Creek Pathway, 5.5 mi N of Luther via State Road; often fills up in summer. Sites 20-26 are walk-in tent sites on a small river peninsula. Undeveloped boat launch off the parking lot for paddlers and anglers (brown and rainbow trout). The Lincoln Hills cycle/ATV trails and ORV routes adjoin the campground. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The campground and seasonal roads are not plowed.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: 26 sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (no length posted); sites 20-26 are walk-in (35 to 60 yards from the parking lot) on a small peninsula, so 19 are drive-in.

name: Mio Pond State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on the west side of Mio Pond, the Au Sable River impoundment at Mio Dam; secluded wooded sites. A separate paddle-in group camp sits on the east side. Managed by Rifle River Recreation Area. 2 mi NW of Mio via Morenci Avenue, Pond Drive and South Gerber Road. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $20 a night per individual site (DNR amenity table). A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: 24 individual wooded campsites 'for tents and small trailers' on the west side (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). A separate group camp of 10 paddle-in sites is on the east side of the pond.

name: Pretty Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic campground in the Pretty Lake Quiet Area (non-motorized use only on Pretty Lake and its seven-lake chain), ~25 mi NW of Newberry via M-123 and County Roads 407 and 416. Only the 18 main-loop sites are drive-in; the walk-in/paddle-in sites lie along the Pretty Lake Pathway, with some short portages. Day-use picnic area; carry-in access ~50 yards from the parking area. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Campground roads may not be plowed in winter.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.
field_notes.Sites: 18 drive-in sites in the main loop, 'suitable for tents and trailers of all sizes' (no maximum length posted), plus 8 walk-in/paddle-in sites (#19-26) 0.8-1.5 mi out along the Pretty Lake Pathway and chain of lakes. The amenity table counts the 18.

name: Maple River Campground
note: Private campground on the banks of the Maple River opposite public state land; large riverfront transient sites plus rustic and primitive sites, a boat launch and live bait for fishing. Most numbered sites away from the river are seasonal (operator's site map). --Claude

Fees: +$5/night each adult over 2, children 15 and under free

field_notes.Booking: Reserve with the office (summer phone hours 10am-5pm); sites are not guaranteed and may be reassigned. Check-in 2pm, check-out noon; Friday check-in until 8pm.
field_notes.Fees: 2026 rates for 2 adults and children under 16 per camping unit: 20/30-amp $35, 50-amp $40; rustic sites (no hookups) $30; $5 per extra adult. Seasonal $2,100 a year plus utilities. Deposit $20 per day of the stay; 7-day cancellation notice.
field_notes.Sites: The operator's site map numbers about 65 sites: about 26 transient sites (green) mostly along the river and about 39 seasonal sites (red, numbers 12-50 away from the river).

name: Stony Haven Campground & Cabins
note: Small (8-acre) Christian family campground, owner-run since 1996 (the owners' daughter is taking over after 2025); 48 RV sites (partial & full hookup, 13 seasonal) plus 16 rustic tent sites and cabins. Alcohol and drug free: possession by anyone in the party is cause for eviction without refund. About 1 mile from Stony Lake and 2 miles from Lake Michigan public access; no on-site swimming/lake frontage. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Rustic tent sites open July - Labor Day.
field_notes.Booking: Reserve online (ReservationFriend, the site's 'Reservations' link) or call 231-861-5201. 'All Reservations require a 2 night minimum stay.' Check in or call by 6 PM on arrival day or the site may be released.
field_notes.Fees: Daily rates for 2 adults + dependent children: Standard (20/30-amp electric/water) $35, Deluxe (20/30-amp full hookup) $40, Premium (50-amp full hookup) $50; Basic rustic $25. Extra adults $6 per night (max 4). 20% off Mon-Wed (not holidays) and after Labor Day. Weekly and monthly rates and seasonal sites ($1,800-2,200 May-Oct) also offered.
field_notes.Sites: Homepage: 48 partial and full hookup RV sites plus 16 rustic tent sites (hike-in or park-on; rustic sites open July - Labor Day); the facilities page says 62 sites. 8 rental cabins.

name: Cadillac Woods Campground
note: Private wooded campground on M-115 in Tustin, SE of Cadillac; RV and rustic tent sites plus rental cabins, clubhouse, pool, mini-golf. Open May-Oct; nightly stays, and a discounted monthly rate by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: The operator's site: RV sites (30-amp/water and 30/50-amp/water) start at $45 a night, rustic tent sites $25, cabins $75. On Campspot for Tue 2026-10-27: 30-amp/water site $47 a night, 30/50-amp/water $50; Campspot adds a $3 booking fee once per stay. Discounted monthly rate by phone.
field_notes.Sites: 34 RV and tent sites (27 with 30-amp/water or 30/50-amp/water, the rest rustic tent sites) plus 6 cabins. The operator says rigs to 42 ft; Campspot lists the 30-amp/water sites to 34 ft and the rustic sites to 30 ft.

name: North Park Campground
note: City of Harbor Beach municipal park (city-owned since 1903) on 40 acres at the north end of town, across N. Huron Ave (M-25) from Lake Huron; full-hookup modern sites, rustic sites in the woods, tent and group camping, nature trail, ball fields. Sites reported tightly spaced. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations by phone to the campground (989-479-9554) from January 1; full payment plus the $8 reservation fee by credit card when booking. Sites are assigned by staff when the reservation is paid; specific sites can't be guaranteed. Holiday and festival weekends are sold prepaid as a block: 3 nights for Memorial Day and Labor Day, 2 nights for July 4th, Maritime Festival and Halloween weekends.
field_notes.Fees: City of Harbor Beach 2026 camping fees (one rate, no resident/non-resident split): RV/trailer under 30 ft $45, over 30 ft $46 ($50/$51 on holidays), rates including water, electric and sewer; pop-up or tent $36, rustic $29. Weekly $260/$270, monthly $660/$710, 6-month seasonal $2,400/$2,500. Cable $3/day on some sites; dump station $10. Prepaid holiday weekends: 3 nights Memorial Day and Labor Day, 2 nights July 4th, Maritime Festival and Halloween weekends.
field_notes.Sites: 184 sites: full-hookup modern, tent and group, and rustic sites in the woods; 24 more around the ball fields due mid-summer 2026. The 2025 map marks 66 sites 'Reserved Seasonal' and about 60 with cable.

name: Craven Park
note: Village of Bellaire campground on Craven Pond, a mile east of downtown; full-hookup, water/electric and rustic sites, a walking loop nearby. Google Maps gives wrong directions: the entrance is at the end of E Broad St where it meets S Derenzy (Fairground) Rd. Camp host at site 30. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Sites 22-25 and 31-35 are first-come only (pay by envelope at the bathhouse); all others are reservation-only, booked online (Firefly) or at the village office, 202 N Bridge St, Mon-Thu 8-4. Same-day campers wanting a reservable site must book it online before setting up. After two weeks campers must leave for a week, except monthly or seasonal stays.
field_notes.Fees: Village of Bellaire rates effective May 6, 2026: water/electric $30 a night, full hookup $40; rustic (primitive) sites $20, left out of the base. One rate for everyone (no resident rate stated). Full hookup only for monthly ($755) and seasonal ($5,000) stays. Non-camper dump $10.

name: Gladstone Bay Campground
note: City of Gladstone campground at 37 Michigan Ave on Little Bay de Noc (Lake Michigan), with a 1,500-ft sandy beach and deck, a boardwalk and bike path, and a playground. Full-hookup, water-and-electric, electric-only and tent sites, with a mix of transient and seasonal campers. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Call the Campground to make Reservations 906-428-1211' (camp@gladstonemi.org). The button on the city page opens the city's Rec1 catalog, which sells facility rentals, boat-launch permits and programs but lists no campsites.
field_notes.Fees: Electric-only sites $30 a day, water and electric $35, full hookup $40; tent sites $20; weekly and monthly rates too. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Brookside Park
note: City of Otsego municipal campground at the back of Brookside Park off M-89 along the Kalamazoo River. RV sites have concrete pads; water comes from 2 spigots shared across 3 sites (bring a splitter); a couple of tent sites too. Register and pay in person at the Otsego Police Department (127 Court St). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Not reservable; register at the Otsego Police Department, 127 Court St. (non-emergency line (269) 692-6111, office hours Mon-Thu 7-5; after hours calls go to Allegan County dispatch).
field_notes.Fees: Otsego Police Department fee list: $30 a night for a cement (RV) site, $20 for a tent site (left out of the base). Paid at the Police Department, cash or check only.

name: Groveland Oaks County Park Campground
note: Oakland County Parks campground on Stewart Lake, 14555 Dixie Hwy, Holly; concrete or gravel pads, plus camping cabins, yurts and 12 group areas. Swimming beach, mini golf, skate park, paved trails. Daily/annual Oakland County vehicle permit required. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: Book online (Oakland County Parks WebTrac) or by phone (248-858-1400 / park 248-634-9811), 180 days ahead. 'Reservations that include a Friday or Saturday must be two nights minimum'; holidays three nights. Check-in 3 p.m. (none after 9 p.m.), check-out 1 p.m. Changes and cancellations by phone or in person only.
field_notes.Fees: 2026 rates (non-resident): water/electric $43, water/electric pull-through $48, full hookup $53, full-hookup pull-through $58; +$5/night on holiday weekends and special events. Oakland County residents pay $5 less Sunday-Thursday (non-holiday): $38/$43/$48/$53. Monthly: 20% off for 30 consecutive days on one site. $10 fee to change or cancel a reservation.
field_notes.Sites: Pull-throughs: full-hookup sites 1-5 and water/electric sites 127, 129, 131, 133. Also 12 group areas, camping cabins and yurts.

name: Caseville County Park
note: Huron County Parks (county government) campground, 6400 Main St, Caseville, on Saginaw Bay (Lake Huron), with one of the state's nicer beaches; the town's shops are walkable. Electric & water, full-hookup and lakefront full-hookup nightly sites plus seasonal and mobile-home sites; pavilions and a playscape. Tents not allowed on full-hookup sites. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked online through Huron County Parks' Checkfront page or by phone (888-265-2583). The next season opens to the public around December 1 (2026 season: Dec 1, 2025, noon). Holiday weekends need 3 consecutive nights. No cancellations within 30 days or over holidays/special events. Seasonal sites go each January to the Seasonal Interest List; parks are at capacity for seasonals.
field_notes.Fees: Huron County Parks, 2026: electric and water $55 a night, full hookup $73, full hookup lakefront $78; each +$5 on holidays and -$5 in the off season. Seasonal sites from $4,600. One rate for everyone (no resident/non-resident split posted). $15 cancellation fee.

name: Maple Grove City Park Campground
note: City of Lake City park on 52 semi-wooded acres at 5547 W. Davis Road, four blocks east of Miltner Beach on Lake Missaukee (inland, not lakefront); playground, ball field, open green space and an 18-hole disc golf course with concrete tee pads. Many sites go to monthly and seasonal campers, so call ahead for a summer weekend. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve by calling the city (231-839-4561 office, 231-839-4429 field); bookings for a season open April 1 and are taken first come, first served. Payment due before check-in.
field_notes.Fees: 2024 season: $35 a night per site, $500 a month, or $475 a month for a season (May through October 1) paid in advance; 5-month stays get a discount. One rate for everyone (no resident/non-resident split). Payment is due before check-in. No 2025 or 2026 rate card is posted.
field_notes.Sites: 'Over 30 campsites', semi-wooded. Many go to monthly and seasonal campers: the city's 2024-04-15 availability sheet showed 3 (July 1) to 17 (May 15-18) sites open on summer dates.

name: Fox Park
note: Cedarville Township park on M-35 along the Bay of Green Bay: 10 acres with a picnic area and beach, about 29 miles north of Menominee. Not part of the Menominee County Parks system, though booked through its reservation site. One camper plus one tent (or two tents) per site. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked on the Menominee County Parks reservation site, but cancellations and questions go to Cedarville Township's contact (906-424-0590): a full refund less the $10 fee 14+ days out, none after.
field_notes.Fees: Electric sites $30 a night; $10 non-refundable reservation fee per site per reservation. No vehicle entrance pass is needed: Fox Park is not part of the Menominee County Parks System.
field_notes.Sites: 22 electric sites (21 listed for booking: 2-16, 17A/B, 18A/B, 19, 20); 14 of the 21 are marked 'Water Frontage'. None are seasonal.

name: St. James Township Campground (Beaver Island)
note: St. James Township campground on a bluff overlooking Lake Michigan and Garden, Squaw and Whiskey Islands, just off Donegal Bay Rd about a mile from the St. James ferry dock at the end of the bike path; a short walk to town and the Donegal Bay swimming beach. Beaver Island is reached only by the Beaver Island Boat Co. car ferry from Charlevoix: only the Emerald Isle carries vehicles (limits 13'6" tall, 46 ft long, 50 tons, so a motorhome fits), and the vehicle space must be reserved by phone. 2026 fare for a vehicle over 7'6" tall and 10 ft long: from $110.41 each way (call with dimensions for the exact price), plus $33.50 per adult each way. Dark-sky viewing area; take care near the bluff. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Full season from the week before Memorial Day weekend; showers close September 30, and rustic winter camping is allowed at a reduced price from October 1 until the spring opening.
field_notes.Booking: Booked online on the township's Firefly Reservations page, or through the campground host at 231-497-4477. Full refund of site fees for cancellations two weeks or more before arrival (by email to the host). A vehicle needs its own Beaver Island Boat Co. ferry reservation, which the township says to secure first.
field_notes.Fees: Non-electric sites $20 a night, electric $30 (township rate sheet, Nov 2024; the township's Firefly booking page quoted the same for 2026-10-25). Rustic winter camping Oct 1 until spring opening at a reduced price (amount not posted). $3.50 reservation fee, not refunded on cancellation. No resident/non-resident split posted.
field_notes.Sites: 12 non-electric sites (1-12) and 5 electric (14-18; there is no site 13). Sites 1-4 and 7 are tent-only (7 is walk-in); RV-capable sites per the booking page: 5, 6, 9, 10 up to 20 ft, 8, 11, 12 and electric 14-16 up to 25 ft, ADA electric sites 17-18 (concrete pads) up to 28 ft. Four people per site (single families or youth groups may be larger).

name: Pentoga Park
note: Iron County park on Chicagon Lake (1630 County Rd 424, Crystal Falls). Beach (no lifeguard) with a changing house, waterfront cook stoves, playground; historic Chippewa (Ojibwa) burial grounds preserved on site. Opens the Friday before Memorial Day through September. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: The Friday before Memorial Day through September.
field_notes.Booking: Book online on Iron County Parks' reservation site or by phone ('Call for reservations', 906-265-3979). Check in at the office before setting up. Cancelling 30+ days out is refunded in full, 7-30 days 50%, under 7 days nothing; refunds come as a voucher.
field_notes.Fees: Iron County, 2026: daily $45, monthly $750, seasonal $2,060 (limited number of seasonal sites); one rate for everyone. A 3% convenience fee on credit-card payments. Reservation fees are non-refundable.
field_notes.Sites: The county's camping page says 134 sites; the park page and booking home page say 135. One camper per site.

name: Curry Park Campground
note: City of Ironwood campground beside the Gogebic County Fairgrounds on US 2, with shaded sites and a small playground.  9 sites have full hookups and the rest electric only. --Claude

field_notes.Season: 2027: tentatively opens Wednesday May 19, closes Sunday October 10.
field_notes.Booking: Online only: 'There are no in person or phone reservation options.' 2027 reservations open January 5, 2027.
field_notes.Fees: City of Ironwood 2027 rates: 30-amp electric (no water at site) $35 a night, 50-amp electric $40, full hookup $45; full hookup $260 a week. One rate for everyone (no resident rate stated). Dump station and water fill included for campers ($15 each for non-guests). Campspot quoted the 2026 rates at $30-40.
field_notes.Sites: 44 shaded sites for RV or tent: 9 full hookup, the rest 30- or 50-amp electric only.
